method.description: Opened each exact supplied PDF in desktop Acrobat Reader, expanded its signature root, inspected the full visible Signatures panel, opened native Signature Properties, clicked Validate Signature, and transcribed the resulting text. G was closed, reopened and validated again after A-F; its result was unchanged.
method.propertyTranscription: Message wording preserved; surrounding whitespace removed. Full status line includes the displayed signing time. Decorative images, memory addresses, dialog controls and generic section titles are omitted.
method.changeCategories: No modification-category rows were displayed in the expanded Signatures panel for any file. This is a UI observation, not a claim that Acrobat has no internal categories. The field-location line is recorded separately.
method.screenshots: Inspected in the interactive session; no standalone screenshot files saved.

settings.applicationPreferences: Same Acrobat session and verification preferences as the v3 corpus run; no settings changed.

interpretation.observed: A-F are INVALID with altered/corrupted wording. G is UNKNOWN because the signer is untrusted, but its document is reported unchanged. The G result repeated before and after testing A-F.
interpretation.supportedInference: Rewriting a page or sealed widget is not necessary to trigger this rejection: the supplied F variant also fails although it only appends a new unreferenced object. The cause is shared more broadly by the appended variants.
interpretation.notEstablished: This does not isolate the ebook base alone as the root cause. The base, signature/revision structure, and common incremental serialization remain possible factors. It does not establish a universal identical-page/widget rewrite rule.
